span_id: Folk and traditional lead-oxide powders; Toxicology; Exposure framing
source_document: karwowski2016-folk-diaper-powder-infant-lead | doi 10.1007/s10653-016-9881-6 — full text replaces abstract-only record. Pb corrected 62 to 62-64 wt% (620,000-639,500 mg/kg); Sb 1000 to 1005 mg/kg body figure; Bi 110 mg/kg added; gastric/lung/urine bioaccessibility percentages added; blood lead 13-18 then 8 ug/dL.

span_id: Folk and traditional lead-oxide powders; Implications
source_document: lin2012-guangzhou-hongdan-baby-powder-lead | doi 10.1016/j.cca.2012.03.010 — third folk case. Case powder >100,000 mg/kg Pb by XRF and 214,000 by FAAS; purchased averages 817,000 (n=16) and 207,000 (n=13); 41 of 48 drugstores stocked a similar powder. Held out of all commercial occurrence statements.

span_id: Source-by-source inventory; Toxicology; Implications for manufacturers
source_document: krekeler2022-baby-powder-nickel-chromium-abstract | doi 10.1130/abs/2022NC-374622 — one 1985 bottle at approximately 2000 ppm Ni and 500 ppm Cr, excluded from every range per ingest ledger item G5-KREKELER-ABSTRACT. Mineral-host observation retained.

rehman2013-talcum-powder-heavy-metals-pakistan (no DOI; researchbib 3425) and nnorom2011-nigeria-facial-talcum-trace-metals | doi 10.1080/02772248.2011.577075 — both recorded, neither promoted. Rehman: unstated digest volume, no baby/adult split. Nnorom: predominantly adult facial talc, three-product baby subgroup not transcribed on the source page.

span_id: Zinc dermal pathway evidence; Abstract; Implications for parents
source_document: fujita2021-hyperzincemia-zno-diaper-dermatitis-infant | doi 10.1111/ped.14761 - second infant case. 10% zinc oxide ointment; serum Zn 77, 119, 490, 194, 82 ug/dL on days 22, 29, 38, 44, 49; stated normal range 58-74; fully breastfed with no zinc supplements, which removes the concurrent-oral-zinc confounder that limited the Yasugi case.

derry1983-zinc-oxide-ointment-absorption and agren1990-zinc-oxide-percutaneous-absorption-man | doi 10.1159/000247982 - intact adult skin. Derry: 100 g of 40% ZnO moved mean serum Zn 107.3+/-5.32 to 116.1+/-5.02 ug/dL at 1 h, reported not significant; petrolatum control fell 115.2 to 103.5. Agren 1990: 25% ZnO occlusive dressing, epidermis 35 to 187 ug/g dry weight, blister fluid 0.27 to 0.95 ug/ml, flux 5 ug/cm2/h, in vitro release 0.54+/-0.01 at pH 5.4 against 0.04+/-0.04 at pH 7.4. Agren 1990 is a different paper from Agren 1991 already cited.

span_id: Abstract; Regulatory landscape; Implications for regulators; Data gaps
source_document: fda2021-otc-monograph-m016-skin-protectant - operative order OTC000005, effective 2020-03-27, posted 2021-09-24. Zinc oxide 1-25 percent, above 25 to 40 percent in an ointment only, no heavy-metal contaminant limit. Closes the retrieval gap previously logged for the operative post-2020 text and replaces reliance on the 1990 proposed rule.

span_id: Product anatomy; Zinc dermal pathway evidence
source_document: stamatas2014-diaper-dermatitis-review and berg1994-diaper-dermatitis-wetness-ph - no metal values. Stamatas: marketed ointments at 13 and 40 percent zinc oxide. Berg: four pooled trials, 1601 infants, diapered skin wetter and higher pH than adjacent undiapered skin. Cited only for the release-environment inference, with the direction stated (higher pH gave less zinc release in the one pH experiment on file).

span_id: Product anatomy; Implications for regulators; Data gaps
source_document: yu2016-diaper-product-potential-allergens and kosemund2009-superabsorbent-diaper-safety - no metal values. Yu: botanical extracts in 30 of 41 topical diaper preparations, fragrance in 18, named as a candidate lead entry route for the unmeasured non-zinc-oxide comparison group rather than as a measurement. Kosemund: manufacturer diaper safety evaluation reporting no Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Cr, Sn or Sb concentration.

span_id: The mineral filters: adult human skin, in vivo
source_document: gulson2010-zno-sunscreen-dermal-zinc and gulson2012-zinc-sunscreen-dermal-absorption - 68Zn isotope tracer in living adults. 2010: 20 adults, 19 nm and 110 nm ZnO, 5 outdoor days, 3.7-5.3 mg/cm2, small tracer rises in blood and urine, chemical form crossing skin not determined. 2012 pilot: ~30 nm ZnO at 52 percent 68Zn, twice daily 5 days without UV, absorption 0.01 percent of applied dose; the less-than glyph ambiguity is carried as recorded at ingest.

span_id: The mineral filters: excised or reconstructed; damaged, occluded and impaired skin
source_document: holmes2016-zinc-oxide-skin-penetration, holmes2020-nano-zinc-oxide-skin and leite-silva2016-nano-zinc-oxide-skin-occlusion - 10 percent ZnO at 10 mg/cm2 on heat-separated human epidermis did not penetrate intact viable epidermis; receptor zinc 0.07 ug/mL at 48 h; zinc within skin about 3.5-fold higher in impaired than intact skin in sweat and about 3-fold in triglyceride; 10 percent w/v at 2 mg/cm2 for 6 h did not penetrate intact or barrier-impaired skin with or without occlusion.

span_id: The mineral filters: animal skin; adult human skin, in vivo
source_document: monteiro-riviere2011-sunscreen-nanoparticle-skin and filipe2009-tio2-zno-stratum-corneum - pig skin with moderate UVB sunburn, four formulations, Ti in perfusate below 0.1 ug/mL and below 0.1 percent of applied dose, Zn matching untreated controls. Filipe: adults, Ti and Zn high in stratum corneum falling to undetectable Ti and physiological Zn below, with no subcorneal Ti signal after 48 h occlusion or tape stripping. Pig skin kept explicitly apart from human and infant skin.

span_id: The mineral filters: damaged, occluded and impaired skin
source_document: larese-filon2015-nanoparticle-skin-absorption-review and schneider2018-inorganic-uv-filters-zno-tio2 - reviews, size framing only. Adopted ranges 4-20 nm for intact and damaged skin and 21-45 nm for damaged skin; nanoparticle designation below 100 nm. No original survey; cited penetration studies not re-extracted.

span_id: Measured evidence: the rest of the measured record; by-metal table; Data gaps
source_document: zmozinski2016-sunscreen-pb-cr, zachariadis2009-sunscreens-trace-elements-icpaes and ali2023-lahore-sunblocks-heavy-metals - three surveys of sunscreens not identified as baby or mineral-only, reported as context and excluded from the seven-unit table and every range. Zmozinski: 11 Brazilian products, total Cr 0.10-0.65 ug/g, total Pb 0.027-1.75 ug/g. Zachariadis: 5 Greek products, Ti 8.13e3 and 18.5e3 ug/g, Pb below a 3.2 ug/g detection limit that sits above the highest baby-unit Pb of 2.14 ug/g, so its nulls are not an upper bound. Ali: 15 Lahore sunblocks, Cr and As not detected without a limit, Table 1 cells cited by code only, no range or maximum drawn because abstract, narrative and Table 1 disagree.

guin2001-baby-wipe-dermatitis, fields2006-contact-dermatitis-baby-wipes, boyapati2013-mi-baby-wipes-hand-dermatitis, admani2014-mi-wet-wipes-perianal, cahill2014-mi-allergy-wipes-australia, chang2014-methylisothiazolinone-baby-wipes, warshaw2017-wet-wipe-allergens-nacdg - seven clinical allergic-contact-dermatitis reports naming a baby or wet wipe as the source, all attributing the reaction to a preservative or fragrance rather than a metal. Cited to support a sentence already on the page; no occurrence finding changed. vanneste2013-methylisothiazolinone-wet-wipes kept separate as household wipes.

celeiro2015-baby-wipes-fragrance-phthalates, yu2016-diaper-product-potential-allergens, hamann2019-methylisothiazolinone-leave-on - ingredient screens and analytical methods, no elemental results. Hamann: no isothiazolinone in any of 31 and 44 unique baby wipe products at two retailers, against 5.4 to 6.6 percent of lotions and 6.8 to 12.2 percent of sunscreens.

obriain2020-wet-wipe-microplastic-fibres, nacci2025-disposable-wet-wipes, pack2021-preservatives-dishwashing-wet-wipes - fibre composition, environmental fate and a preservative survey, none reporting a metal concentration. Nacci and Pack are not identified as baby wipes and Nacci's polypropylene-or-polyester finding is explicitly not read against the polyester-catalyst account in section 4.
